source_text:
HISTORY: Smoking history 50-pack years of smoking.

INDICATION: Dyspnea.

PROCEDURE: FVC was 59%. FEV1 was 45%. FEV1/FVC ratio was 52%. The predicted was 67%. FEF 25/75% was 22%, improved about 400-cc, which represents 89% improvement with bronchodilator. SVC was 91%. Inspiratory capacity was 70%. Residual volume was 225% of its predicted. Total lung capacity was 128%.

IMPRESSION:
1. Moderate obstructive lung disease with some improvement with bronchodilator indicating bronchospastic element.
2. Probably there is some restrictive element because of fibrosis. The reason for that is that the inspiratory capacity was limited and the total lung capacity did not increase to the same extent as the residual volume and expiratory residual volume.
3. Diffusion capacity was not measured. The flow volume loop was consistent with the above.

adjudication_notes: Adjudicated from SC (Person 1) and RP (Person 2). Both captured the same spirometry values (FVC 59%, FEV1 45%, FEV1/FVC 52%, predicted 67%, FEF 25/75% 22% improved ~400 cc = 89% with bronchodilator, SVC 91%, inspiratory capacity 70%, residual volume 225% predicted, total lung capacity 128%) and the impression (moderate obstructive lung disease with a bronchospastic element; probable restrictive element from fibrosis; diffusion capacity not measured; flow-volume loop consistent). Both annotators recorded the 50-pack-year smoking history, so it is included (typed diagnosis). Type conflicts resolved toward lab_value (agreeing with RP): 'diffusion capacity was not measured' and 'flow volume loop consistent' -- these are measurement statements, not procedures. RP's two explanatory sub-findings (inspiratory capacity limited; total lung capacity did not increase to the same extent as RV/ERV) were added since they are explicitly stated. SC's combined FEF fact (value + improvement + percent) was kept rather than RP's three-way split; no information differs. F6 ('The predicted was 67%') preserves the report's ambiguity about which parameter is predicted. Uncertainty ('Probably ... restrictive element') and negation ('not measured') preserved.
